items.headline: Alphabet falls 11-12% after a capex-heavy quarter leaves free cash flow negative for a second straight quarter
items.why: Cloud revenue grew 103%, yet the market punished the stock because AI spending is now being funded with about $28.7B of new debt and $12.4B of stock sales, which makes the payback on the buildout the central question for mega-cap tech.

sources.title: Alphabet sinks as AI spending pushes cash flow negative again (24/7 Wall St.)

items.headline: Microsoft reports quarterly capex of $45.2B, below consensus, and says demand still exceeds available supply
items.why: The shortfall was blamed on delayed third-party capacity, so spending is supply-limited rather than demand-limited, which pushes some of the buildout into later quarters instead of cancelling it.

sources.title: Amazon slides as Alphabet plunge raises stakes for AWS report (24/7 Wall St.)

items.headline: Meta rises about 3% while its AI-peers fall, after lifting the low end of 2026 capex guidance to $135-145B
items.why: Meta was the only large AI spender to gain on the week's results because its spending is funded mostly by advertising revenue (up 26% year on year) rather than by new debt, which is the distinction the market is now pricing.

sources.title: Amazon slides as Alphabet plunge raises stakes for AWS report (24/7 Wall St.)

items.headline: The world's largest crypto exchange loses about $6.3B in a hack, the largest theft in crypto history
items.why: Issuers have frozen roughly $3B of the stolen stablecoins and the exchange says it will cover all losses from its own reserves, so the market risk is a liquidity and confidence shock rather than customer insolvency, with attribution pointing to a state-linked attacker.

sources.title: Crypto Market Update: record US$6.3 billion hack (Investing News Network)

items.headline: Bitcoin falls about 5% in 24 hours to roughly $77.6K and Ether drops about 5% to roughly $2,230 on the hack news
items.why: The sell-off landed alongside a sharp tech-stock decline, so crypto is trading as a risk asset tied to equities rather than as a haven, and the price reaction to the hack was fast but not disorderly.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with two dissenters wanting a hike
items.why: Markets price roughly an 83-85% chance of a quarter-point hike at the December 8-9 meeting, so the policy debate has moved from when to cut to whether to tighten further.

items.headline: Hot data backs the hawks: Q3 GDP grew 3.4%, September PCE inflation rose to 3.6% year on year, and the 10-year yield sits near 5%
items.why: Growth beating expectations while inflation re-accelerates removes the argument for easing, and a 10-year yield at 5% raises borrowing costs across the economy and competes directly with equities and non-yielding assets.

items.headline: Strait of Hormuz stays unresolved: a commercial tanker was hit by explosives on Friday while regional mediators work to restart US-Iran talks
items.why: About a fifth of seaborne oil moves through the strait, so each escalation or diplomatic headline feeds directly into crude and then into the inflation numbers the Fed is reacting to.

items.why: Oil is the single biggest driver of this week's inflation worries and of the hawkish Fed tone, so the Hormuz risk premium is now a macro variable rather than a pure energy story.
